Configure maturity probability

Source: R/sim_biology.R
sim_maturity.Rd

Uses the same logistic calculation as sim_logistic(), with defaults for a historical maturity-at-length relationship rather than survey catchability.

sim_maturity(k = 0.28, x50 = 47.81, plot = FALSE)

Arguments

k

Nonnegative steepness, in inverse units of the input trait.

x50

Trait value at 50 percent maturity: length or age according to maturity_by in sim_abundance().

plot

Logical. Plot when the returned function is used?

Value

A function of x returning probabilities in [0, 1]. Interchangeable with sim_logistic() when parameters and trait basis agree.

Details

Defaults approximate the female 3Ps cod relationship for 1996 in Table 3 of Brattey and Morgan (1996), DFO Atlantic Fisheries Research Document 96/92: https://waves-vagues.dfo-mpo.gc.ca/Library/198884.pdf. Length is in centimetres and k is approximately 0.28 per centimetre. Maturity varies by sex and period; this historical example is not a contemporary stock calibration. SimSurvey applies one curve to all fish, without a female fraction. Maturity is a probability, not a knife-edge classification at x50. Supply age-appropriate k and x50 when using age-based maturity.

Examples

maturity <- sim_maturity()
maturity(c(30, 47.81, 60))
#> [1] 0.006781179 0.500000000 0.968114531
